core.title: Bind each acceptance to exactly one metric_id
core.given: A planner is authoring or editing an acceptance or plan artifact, or placing/moving a plan artifact's acceptances, tests or artifacts.
core.when: The plan artifact, test or artifact is written or moved.
core.then: Bind each acceptance to exactly one metric_id from the dimension-to-metric_id table of the metric-mapping rule, matching its parent plan artifact's dimension.
prefer: Take the metric_id from the metric-mapping row for the parent plan artifact's dimension.
Write a separate acceptance for each additional measure.
Mandatory on every plan-artifact create/edit: declare exactly one dimension and one lens_ref.
Mandatory on every placement/move: put the plan artifact, its acceptances, tests and artifacts in the plan artifact's own location, so history and review of the plan artifact stay in one place.
avoid: Mixed measures: one acceptance binding more than one metric_id.
A metric_id not in the metric-mapping table.
A plan artifact without exactly one dimension and one lens_ref.
A plan artifact's acceptances, tests or artifacts placed apart from the plan artifact.
core.why: Keeping the plan artifact, its acceptances, tests and artifacts together keeps their history and review cohesive.
evidence: Each acceptance declares exactly one metric_id, listed in the metric-mapping rule's dimension-to-metric_id table under the parent plan artifact's dimension.
Each plan artifact declares exactly one dimension and one lens_ref.
The plan artifact, its acceptances, tests and artifacts live together in the plan artifact's location.
verification: Metric binding: each acceptance maps to exactly one metric_id drawn from the metric-mapping rule's dimension-to-metric_id table; one acceptance binding more than one metric_id (mixed measures) fails.
The metric-mapping table is the sole source of valid metric_ids for this check; editing the table itself is out of scope here (governed by the metric-mapping rule).
Lens/dimension dependency: exactly one dimension and one lens_ref per plan artifact; checked on every plan-artifact create/edit, not only when acceptance metrics change.

Collocation: checked on every placement/move of the plan artifact or any of its acceptances, tests or artifacts — including test-only or artifact-only changes — by comparing each member's path with its owning plan artifact's location.

Enforcement needs a diff-level observer over acceptance metric_id fields, plan-artifact dimension/lens_ref declarations, and the paths of a plan artifact's acceptances, tests and artifacts relative to the owning plan artifact (needs_new_observer).

fires: Planner authors a new acceptance under a plan artifact
Planner edits an acceptance so its measured quantity or metric_id changes, or adds a second measure
Planner creates a plan artifact or adds/changes its dimension or lens_ref, with no acceptance metric change
Planner places or moves a plan artifact or its acceptances to a different location
Planner adds or moves only a test or artifact belonging to a plan artifact, with no acceptance or plan-artifact file change
doesNotFire: Coder edits implementation code without touching acceptance or plan-artifact artifacts, plan-artifact-owned tests or artifacts, or their locations
Editing prose docs unrelated to acceptances or plan artifacts
Editing the metric-mapping table itself (governed by the metric-mapping rule)

neutralityNotes: The rule is method-level rather than stack-mechanical, so it neutralizes cleanly. 'WMBT' is the Bun plan-artifact kind and becomes 'plan artifact' in the core, instantiated per stack through roles.plan_artifact.kinds (no proposed key needed). ATDD-method vocabulary is kept as stack-neutral: acceptance, metric_id, dimension, lens_ref, planner, coder. Cross-references to the concrete metric-mapping rule id (planner.criteria.metric-mapping), the metric catalog URN (conventions:criteria:metrics) and the tester template registry path are realization-level and live only in bunOnly; the core refers to 'the metric-mapping rule/table' by name, and each stack must bind that name to its own metric-mapping rule id when instantiating (the same applies to the doesNotFire entry about editing the catalog). The activation fact notes were preserved in fires and in the verification array because the core fact schema carries no note field. doesNotFire[0] rephrases the source's 'acceptance/WMBT artifacts, WMBT-owned tests/artifacts' without the slash-separated pairings to keep path-like fragments out of the core text; the meaning is unchanged. No conditions were dropped or added: unless stays empty and the two secondary obligations (single dimension/lens_ref, collocation) remain mandatory prefer/avoid steps with unchanged activation.
